text.p: Florida Rock Industries Inc said Wednesday it expects the results for fiscal 1997 to show substantial improvement over last year's results.

The company said that given the strong levels of construction activity that were maintained during the normally depressed second quarter, it does not anticipate the usual very strong improvement in the third quarter as compared with the second.

Florida Rock reported earnings for the second quarter ended March 31, 1997 of $0.70 a share, compared with $0.29 a share for the previous second quarter. Sales were $101.6 million versus $85.8 million.

According to the comapny, the increase in net sales was primarily attributed to the very mild weather in its non-Florida markets, where there was only limited curtailment of construction activity due to inclement weather or freezing temperatures.
Last year's severe winter stopped construction for extended periods of time, the company said.
It said that sales also increased as the result of modest price increases, much of which were in response to higher cement and other cost increases.
Construction activity remains at good levels in the majority of its markets and vacancy rates remain at low to reasonable levels, Flordia Rock said.
The company said that rising interest rates have yet to depress activity as demand continues to be the major driver of activity.
However, the company said that if rates continued to rise they would start to dampen construction activity.
